raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Follow-up to #8933 (review feedback from @0z5a).

## Background

#8933 made the HybridEngine graph capture gate device-agnostic: instead of matching the device name, it admits every accelerator whose `create_graph()` returns a graph. That is CUDA and NPU, but also HPU (`HPUGraph`), MLU (`MLUGraph`) and SUPA (`SUPAGraph`).

Only CUDA and NPU implement `is_current_stream_capturing()`. `DeepSpeedStaticCache.update` relies on it to skip the per-row write-position bounds check (`(cache_position < 0).any()`) while capturing. On the other backends the check would run during capture and synchronize the host, which is illegal while a stream is being captured, and none of those backends is in the test matrix. Before #8933, the device-name check kept them on the eager fallback.

## Change

- Add `is_graph_capture_supported()` to the accelerator interface. The default is `False`, so backends opt in explicitly, and only after they implement `is_current_stream_capturing()`.
- Override it to `True` for CUDA and NPU.
- Use it in both graph capture gates: `validate_graph_capture_support()` in `hybrid_engine_graph.py` and the continuous rollout path in `hybrid_engine_rollout.py`.
- Update the affected unit tests and add a case that a backend exposing `create_graph()` without the opt-in stays on eager decode.

HPU, MLU and SUPA keep the eager fallback with the existing warning. They can be enabled later by implementing the stream-capture query and validating the path.

## Testing

Branch `fix-hybrid-engine-graph-capture-opt-in`, HEAD `9427e0d55` (parent `2d80cedd2`), working tree clean. Both on-device runs use this commit.

### CUDA (8×A100-SXM4-80GB, single card used; torch 2.14.1+cu126, CUDA 12.6, Python 3.10.22; transformers 4.57.6)

- Gate: `CUDA_Accelerator.is_graph_capture_supported()` returns True and CPU returns False.
- `validate_graph_capture_support()`: allows ZeRO-2 and rejects ZeRO-3.
- `DecodeGraphCache`: all 4 decode positions captured, the host forward runs exactly once per position; the same length reuses graphs, a length change recaptures, and exceeding `max_positions` raises.
- End-to-end generate (local tiny GPT-J): 2 inference containers, capture active, 7/7 positions captured, graph output identical to eager.
- Deprecated alias `enable_cuda_graph: true`: warning emitted, capture active, output identical.
- Official OPT E2E passes with transformers 4.44.2 (legacy tuple cache).
- No regression observed.

Suite results (transformers 4.57.6, default marker selection):

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_he_graph.py` | 21 passed |
| `test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py` | 50 passed |
| `test_accelerator_graph.py` | 1 passed, 1 skipped (CUDA has graph support; the eager-fallback case is skipped by design) |
| `test_accelerator.py` | 35 passed |
| **Total** | **107 passed, 1 skipped** |

### NPU (Ascend 910B4; torch 2.10 + torch_npu 2.10.0.post7)

- Unit tests on the changed gate with transformers 5.19.0: `pytest tests/unit/hybrid_engine/test_he_graph.py tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py -q -m "not seq_inference"` — 70 passed, 1 skipped (native CUDA kernel test).
- Official OPT E2E passes with transformers 4.44.2 (venv-tf442).
- Full-model end-to-end on the gated paths (validated in #8933): transformers 4.57.6 — GPT-2 continuous graph capture, token-identical 32/32 over 3 runs, 5.97×; transformers 4.44.2 — inference-container graph capture and replay.
- Full-model continuous-path validation uses transformers 4.57.6; 5.x support is tracked separately in #8852.

### Other backends

- HPU, MLU and SUPA are not available here; their fallback is covered by the default-`False` unit test, not an on-device run. CPU was verified to return `False`.

## Conclusion

The implementation behaves correctly with no CUDA regression: the opt-in gate applies per backend, CUDA keeps graph capture, non-opt-in backends fall back to eager decode, and the old config alias remains compatible.

Follow-up to #8933 (review feedback from @0z5a).

## Background

#8933 made the HybridEngine graph capture gate device-agnostic: instead of matching the device name, it admits every accelerator whose `create_graph()` returns a graph. That is CUDA and NPU, but also HPU (`HPUGraph`), MLU (`MLUGraph`) and SUPA (`SUPAGraph`).

Only CUDA and NPU implement `is_current_stream_capturing()`. `DeepSpeedStaticCache.update` relies on it to skip the per-row write-position bounds check (`(cache_position < 0).any()`) while capturing. On the other backends the check would run during capture and synchronize the host, which is illegal while a stream is being captured, and none of those backends is in the test matrix. Before #8933, the device-name check kept them on the eager fallback.

## Change

- Add `is_graph_capture_supported()` to the accelerator interface. The default is `False`, so backends opt in explicitly, and only after they implement `is_current_stream_capturing()`.
- Override it to `True` for CUDA and NPU.
- Use it in both graph capture gates: `validate_graph_capture_support()` in `hybrid_engine_graph.py` and the continuous rollout path in `hybrid_engine_rollout.py`.
- Update the affected unit tests and add a case that a backend exposing `create_graph()` without the opt-in stays on eager decode.

HPU, MLU and SUPA keep the eager fallback with the existing warning. They can be enabled later by implementing the stream-capture query and validating the path.

### CUDA (8×A100-SXM4-80GB, single card used; torch 2.14.1+cu126, CUDA 12.6, Python 3.10.22; transformers 4.57.6)

+subclass of a graph-capable accelerator must override it to `False`. The static KV cache uses that query to skip
+host-side bounds checks while a graph is being recorded, so backends without both hooks
+keep eager generation.

What changed in this PR This follow-up to #8933 adds an explicit accelerator capability gate for HybridEngine graph capture, rather than treating graph creation alone as sufficient support. **Changes:** - Add a default-off capability hook, with CUDA and NPU overrides. - Apply the hook to HybridEngine and rollout graph paths, including eager fallback for standard rollout generation. - Update capability tests and document backend opt-in requirements. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tests/​unit/​runtime/​rollout/​test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py` | Update graph gates and test standard rollout eager fallback. | | `tests/​unit/​hybrid_engine/​test_he_graph.py` | Test explicit opt-in independently of graph creation. | | `docs/​_tutorials/​accelerator-abstraction-interface.md` | Document graph capture capability requirements. | | `deepspeed/​runtime/​rollout/​hybrid_engine_rollout.py` | Gate rollout graph paths on accelerator support. | | `deepspeed/​runtime/​hybrid_engine_graph.py` | Replace graph-creation probing with the capability hook. | | `accelerator/​npu_accelerator.py` | Enable the capability for NPU. | | `accelerator/​cuda_accelerator.py` | Enable the capability for CUDA. | | `accelerator/​abstract_accelerator.py` | Define the default-off capability hook. |
Review effort: Balanced

Read at `cd5d4ad9`. Thanks for following up on this. The opt-in reads well: it defaults to `False` without being abstract, KLXPU opts back out explicitly, and all three entry points (`validate_graph_capture_support`, the non-continuous `generate()`, and `_generate_continuous`) now fall back to eager instead of raising.

One problem on a CPU-only run. `test_he_graph.py`, `test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py` and `tests/unit/accelerator/` give 5 failed / 48 passed / 5 skipped here, against 51 passed / 5 skipped on master. The five are the three `test_continuous_graph_rejects_incompatible_fixed_layout_options` cases, `test_continuous_graph_rejects_flash_attention` and `test_continuous_generation_routes_graph_capture_to_fixed_capacity_path`, which fail with `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'MagicMock'` or `StopIteration`. They don't mock the accelerator, so on CPU the new gate in `_generate_continuous` takes the eager fallback and runs into the mocked engine; on CUDA and NPU the opt-in is `True`, which is why your runs pass. Making the active accelerator opt in for those tests makes all five pass. Patching `get_accelerator` as the neighbouring tests do, or `patch.object(type(get_accelerator()), "is_graph_capture_supported", return_value=True)`, would do it. `cpu-torch-latest` runs the whole `unit/` tree, so it would hit them.

This also conflicts with #8939 in `hybrid_engine_rollout.py`: #8939 drops `and is_greedy` from the same condition so sampled requests use the graph path too. Whichever lands second should keep the opt-in check and drop `is_greedy`.
